text: Townview is a suburb of Mount Isa in the City of Mount Isa, Queensland, Australia. It is classified as a "townside" suburb, located east of the Leichhardt River, which flows north-south through Mount Isa and divides the town into "mineside" (west) and "townside" (east) areas. Townview is bounded to the north by the Barkly Highway. At an elevation of 380 metres (1,250 ft) above sea level, it is slightly more elevated than other parts of Mount Isa, offering views of the town and contributing to its name. The spelling of Townview (commonly written as Town View) was standardised in 2003 at the request of the Mount Isa City Council. Townview State School, a government primary school for boys and girls (Prep–6), opened on 25 January 1965 and is located at 64–72 Clarke Street (20°44′02″S 139°30′26″E / 20.7339°S 139.5073°E). In the 2016 census, Townview had a population of 2,062 people, and in the 2021 census, the population was 2,067. In 2016, the school had 281 students (170 of whom identified as Indigenous Australians), 25 teachers (24 full-time equivalent), and 18 non-teaching staff (13 full-time equivalent); in 2018, enrolment was 233 students (161 Indigenous Australians), with 24 teachers (22 full-time equivalent) and 20 non-teaching staff (15 full-time equivalent). There are no secondary schools in Townview; the nearest government secondary school is Spinifex State College, which has its junior campus in Parkside to the south-west and its senior campus in Pioneer to the north. The area includes several parks. Media related to Townview, Queensland is available at Wikimedia Commons.
